prologue.tagline: Hold up your phone and find the voices from a hundred years ago hidden around Kumamoto University.
prologue.step1.title: Find
prologue.step1.body: Visit 3 places on campus: the Chemistry Laboratory, Goko Café (festival stall) and the Goko Memorial Museum. Any order is fine.
prologue.step2.title: Scan
prologue.step2.body: Scan the QR code with your phone's built-in Camera app.
prologue.step3.title: Claim
prologue.step3.body: Once you have all 3 stamps, exchange them for the prize “Pukuseki (Puku-Ishi)” (a limited balloon) at the Goko Memorial Museum.

prologue.notes.1h: Please don't use in-app cameras such as LINE's
prologue.notes.1b: They can cause your stamp progress to be lost.
prologue.notes.2: Always open the QR code in your phone's standard browser, such as Safari on iPhone or Chrome on Android.

food.hint: A whisper is sleeping somewhere in this stall.
food.where: The stall is between the Goko Memorial Museum and the Bunpo Building, near the roundabout and the Sub Stage. A clue to the “whisper” is hidden on the booth sign or on the cups.
food.about: Goko Café is a food stall run during this year's SIGMA Festival. It is not a historic permanent café.
food.item.akane.name: Akanezora Cream Soda
food.item.akane.title: Akanezora Cream Soda (Sunset Glow)
food.item.akane.short: A glass of sunset-red soda topped with vanilla ice cream.
food.item.akane.desc: A cream soda whose sunset-red color fills the glass. Enjoy the smooth vanilla ice cream paired with refreshing, fizzy bubbles.
food.item.aoi.name: Aozora Cream Soda
food.item.aoi.title: Aozora Cream Soda (Blue Sky)
food.item.aoi.short: A refreshing soda in a clear blue gradient, served with vanilla ice cream.
food.item.aoi.desc: An eye-catching drink that fades from deep blue to sky blue. The cup carries a special commemorative sticker from Goko Café. Enjoy the effervescence and creamy sweetness.
food.item.shin.name: Shinryoku Cream Soda
food.item.shin.title: Shinryoku Cream Soda (Fresh Green)
food.item.shin.short: A nostalgic café classic: vivid emerald green topped with a bright red cherry.
food.item.shin.desc: A classic cream soda recalling Meiji-era Western café culture. Accented with a bright red cherry and an exclusive cat sticker. A perfect refreshment during your walk.
food.item.yugi.name: Yugiri Cream Soda
food.item.yugi.title: Yugiri Cream Soda (Evening Mist)
food.item.yugi.short: A cream soda in soft tones like mist at dusk, served with vanilla ice cream.
food.item.yugi.desc: A cream soda with soft colors like evening mist spreading through the glass. Enjoy a gentle, calming sip of creamy vanilla and light carbonation.

place.chem.summary: A red-brick laboratory. The first voice sleeps in the QR code here.
place.chem.title: Lamp-driven Airflow and the Sunshielding Corridor
place.chem.body: Built in 1889 (Meiji 22) before electricity arrived, this lab used the rising heat of kerosene lamps to vent toxic gases up the chimney—one of Japan's oldest surviving draft chambers (fume hoods). To deflect Kumamoto's intense afternoon sun, a long corridor was constructed solely along the west side.
place.goko.summary: A memorial museum with an arched entrance. The last voice sleeps here.
place.goko.title: Red Brick and Classical Columns
place.goko.body: Its solid red-brick walls, laid in English bond, reach roughly 60 cm in thickness on the first floor. The grand central staircase features graceful Greek-style column carvings, preserving the historic atmosphere where Natsume Soseki and Lafcadio Hearn once lectured.
place.cafe.summary: Go to the Food page for Goko Café (festival stall).
place.relief.summary: A bronze relief carved on the monument.
place.relief.title: The “Kumamoto Spirit” Bestowed upon Students
place.gate.summary: The gate standing at the campus entrance.
place.gate.name: Front Gate (Akamon / Red Gate)
place.gate.title: Through the Stern Gate, Buckwheat in Bloom
place.gate.body: Built around 1889 facing the historic Bungo Road, the front gate was constructed without doors from the very beginning. Passing through the stately red-brick pillars once revealed rustic fields within the campus, prompting Natsume Soseki to write the haiku: 'Through the stern gate, buckwheat in bloom.'
cele.honkan.lines: Wrapped in a hundred years of wind, the red bricks quietly count the passage of time. / Every step of your journey opens a new page in a new era.
cele.honkan.source: Former Fifth High School, Memorial Museum Main Building
cele.hearn.lines: A foreign breeze stirs this garden, yet the heart of old Japan still breathes here. / To you, who turned from hollow luxury and sought pure, honest truth.
cele.soseki.lines: Education forms the bedrock of a nation; mutual harmony between teachers and students is the fountain of growth. / We honor your thoughtful path across a century of wisdom.
cele.soseki.source: From Natsume Soseki's Address at Fifth High School Commemoration Ceremony
cele.tea.lines: In this hall of learning in the Land of Fire, the wisdom of East and West warms and intertwines. / To you, who heard every whisper: our highest praise, and a cup to cheer.
cele.tea.source: A Crossing of Wisdom: Goko Café
place.relief.body: A bronze bas-relief of Lafcadio Hearn standing as if watching over the red-brick Main Building. The stone monument beside it is inscribed with the concluding words of his address to students, urging them to preserve the spirit of Kyushu and Kumamoto—'loving simple strength, simplicity, and goodness.'
whisper.1.lines: Approach through intellect, and edges grow sharp; / Paddle with emotion, and you are swept away. / Force your will, and life becomes confined. / Climbing the mountain path, / Such were the thoughts that stirred my mind.
whisper.2.lines: I am a cat. As yet I have no name. / Where I was born, / I have not the slightest clue; / Yet the lively warmth of this seat of learning / Is most pleasing to my soul.
whisper.3.lines: The spirit of old Japan still breathes here. / O pure and tranquil garden, / The voices of youthful companions / Are carved into these centenary stones.
consent.doc.body:
• We collect: the nickname you set, stamp progress, and technical logs needed to keep the service secure.
• We do not collect: real name, email, phone number, or detailed GPS location.
• Data is used only to run the stamp rally, verify prize exchange, and keep the system stable.
• Server-side records are deleted within 30 days after the festival ends.
• Anonymous statistics (e.g. total participants) may be used in campus museum reports.
• Misuse (inappropriate nicknames, abuse of the system) may result in deletion of records without notice.
• Contact: Campus Museum Promotion Organization, Kumamoto University (email as shown on this screen).
• The Japanese Terms of Use and Privacy Policy are the authoritative text; this is a summary for convenience.
